description: Eliminate WorkflowRun State full-load reads on the task-log path via a write-maintained run-work projection (taskId<->workId map + active-work identity).

tasks.title: Run-work projection read-model (schema, write maintenance, read API)
tasks.description: Add the WorkflowRunTaskMap child table (WorkflowRunId, TaskId, WorkId) with (runId,TaskId) and (runId,WorkId) indexes, plus nullable ActiveWorkId/ActiveWorkerId columns on WorkflowRunRow, via an EF Core migration. Maintain both in WorkflowRunStore.StageRunAsync via a single shared map/active-work helper (rebuilt from all TaskRuns across all stages, WorkId = TaskRun.WorkId ?? Id; active-work columns from the run's current active work), committed in the same transaction as State; clear map rows in DeleteAsync. Expose the State-free reads through a new narrow IWorkflowRunWorkProjection interface (ResolveWorkIdAsync(runId,taskId), ResolveTaskIdAsync(runId,workId), IsActiveWorkAsync(runId,workId,runnerId), GetProjectIdAsync(runId) via existing MetadataProjectId), with a concrete implementation registered in DI. Include unit tests for write-maintenance correctness and a read-API test asserting the implementation reads only projection columns.
acceptanceCriteria: EF migration adds WorkflowRunTaskMap (indexed both directions) and nullable WorkflowRuns.ActiveWorkId/ActiveWorkerId; dotnet build is clean (TreatWarningsAsErrors).

After StageRunAsync saves a run with tasks across multiple stages plus a running task, the persisted map rows equal (runId, task.Id, task.WorkId ?? task.Id) for every task in every stage, and ActiveWorkId/ActiveWorkerId match the run's single current active work (null when none).
Deleting a WorkflowRun removes its WorkflowRunTaskMap rows.

IWorkflowRunWorkProjection is defined and registered in DI; its concrete implementation returns correct results reading only projection columns (unit test asserts the State-deserializing JSON.Deserialize<WorkflowRun> path is not invoked).
The map/active-work computation is a single shared helper reused by StageRunAsync (and later the backfill upgrader), so there is one author of the projection.
tasks.output: Projection schema + EF migration + shared map/active-work helper + StageRunAsync/DeleteAsync maintenance + IWorkflowRunWorkProjection interface + DI registration + concrete read implementation + unit tests
tasks.notes: ActiveWorkId holds either a task workId or the checks workId (checks-<stage>); ActiveWorkerId is the assigned worker. WorkId stored as the effective work id (WorkId ?? Id); note taskId<->workId is identity today (claimed tasks set WorkId = logicalTaskId = Id), so the table's real job is run-scoped task membership, with WorkId carried for robustness. Maintenance is derived from the in-memory run, never by deserializing State on read.

tasks.title: Backfill existing WorkflowRuns projection (cold-start data upgrader)
tasks.description: Add a cold-start C# data upgrader in the database-initialization flow that populates WorkflowRunTaskMap and the active-work columns for every existing WorkflowRuns row by deserializing State once, computing the same map/active-work as StageRunAsync. Make it idempotent (skip already-populated rows), preflight every candidate (deserialize via the current model; abort with no writes if any row fails), batch writes in a single transaction, and order it after the #536 State-format upgrader. Existing terminal runs must end up queryable. Include an idempotence/correctness unit test.
acceptanceCriteria: On a database with pre-existing WorkflowRuns rows, the upgrader populates the map and active-work columns for every row, including terminal runs, so historical log queries remain resolvable.
Re-running the upgrader produces no additional changes (idempotent) and does not rewrite State or advance ETag for rows already populated.
Preflight: a row whose State cannot be deserialized/mapped aborts the upgrader before any write (no partial population); the server does not enter service until migration completes.
Upgrader is ordered after the #536 State-format upgrader in the init flow.
Idempotence + correctness unit test passes; npm test passes.
tasks.output: Cold-start data upgrader + idempotence/correctness unit test
tasks.notes: Follow design/workflow/run-state.md migration discipline: ordered, idempotent, single-transaction, preflight before service. Reuses the shared map/active-work helper extracted in T-001 (single author). This upgrader is itself a State-writing path and must refresh the projection in the same transaction it reads State, per the write-time obligation in design D2.

tasks.title: Switch TaskLogService to the projection (remove all State loads)
tasks.description: Swap TaskLogService's dependency from the concrete WorkflowRunQuerier to IWorkflowRunWorkProjection, and rewrite ResolveWorkIdAsync, IsActiveWorkAsync, and ResolvePublishScopeAsync to call the projection reads, removing all three State deserializations. Publish scope resolves workId->taskId from the map and projectId (only when taskId resolves) from MetadataProjectId; an unmappable workId yields a null scope (no fan-out). The agent-job ownership branch is untouched. Add a spec test using a fake IWorkflowRunWorkProjection to drive upload (active + inactive work) and query (hit + miss), asserting acceptance, publish-scope stamping, null-scope no-fan-out, and empty-page-on-miss behavior are preserved. Because the interface exposes no State-deserializing member, State deserialize is structurally unreachable from TaskLogService.
acceptanceCriteria: TaskLogService depends on IWorkflowRunWorkProjection (not the concrete WorkflowRunQuerier); no State-deserializing member is reachable from the task-log upload or query paths.

Spec test uses a fake IWorkflowRunWorkProjection to verify upload (active->persist, inactive/unknown->4xx) and query (hit->page, miss->empty page) behavior, plus publish-scope stamping (taskId + projectId) for task workIds and a null scope (no fan-out) for unmappable/checks workIds — all identical to the prior contract.
tasks.output: Rewritten TaskLogService read methods + no-State-deserialize spec test
tasks.notes: Must follow T-002: switching over before backfill would make log queries for existing terminal runs return empty pages. This also removes the upload's double-State-load redundancy (two full deserializations -> two indexed lookups for the same run).
